questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The weather and temperature of he destination. As well as it having a contract with my home university to minimize the bureaucracy of the exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wass very different from what i expected. Pisa is a much smaller city compared to many others.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy. I ended up writing multiple emails and goiong in person to an office. In the end i got help from other students through the erasmus student network whatsapp group chat.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. They didn't even send me the email with the welcome event. It was only on instagram.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Used airbnb. Expensive af, but easy also.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I dont know what to tell you. Fiinding housing here iis hard if youre not italian or physically present to see the room. I can recommend using airbnb if you have the budget.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Itt hard to remember a semester later. There was a portal called alice you needed to use and some others. It was a little bit of a 'jungle.'

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Never sought any. Figured it out in the end.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successsful. Except one whehre the prof. "didnt feel like it this semester" so i ended up with only half that course. #italy

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Honestly go for the vibes. Italy is a whole vibe, and one needs to just go with the flow. The hardest thing for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is hard to tell. In one course (DAD) the material was super easy but the exam was super hard. And the other course (ASE) the opposite..

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More immature. Prof. writing in all caps in the teams channel shouting at students for not showing up, at a course where there is not obligatory attendance was shcking to me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: DAD and ASE in department of computer science.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think it doesnt matter. Exchange is not only for academics, it is also for the extracurricular experience. And taking too hard courses prevents the cultural exchange that should ultimately be part of it, right.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets are more expensive than denmark. Also the utilities bill in pisa is crazy high. 145 eur a month on top. Here i includede in the 4900dkk.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets more expensive. Eating out colon less expe

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dontt know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the ESN groupchat. But i dont reccomend going to the events. They are awfully planned. I met all my friends through the chat and then we went on adventures together, without the ESN official events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Ofc the big italian cities that u already know. But also the small cities around pisa. You can get a lot for little money: Livorno Aquarium, Vespa Museum Casciana, Lucca, Viareggio Carnival/beach.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Pisans speak english because of the leaning tower tourists.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No i only hang with internationals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything is chaotic and loud compared to scandi culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Being spontaneous.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Live in the moment. 2. Try to see the positive side of things. 3. Be curious about other cultures.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go out every single day the first 2 weeks, then you can relax. Here all the friendshipsn will be made. You will have a good time! Don't worry.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships we made along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the chaos of italy and other student's culture. e.g. being late, not showing up on time, being spontaneous, not planning. Etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Good luck! You will have a memorable experience and hopefully friends for life in other countries!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
